subtopic: Target Encoding, Target Leakage and Out-of-Fold Encoding
question_text:
### Production Incident Scenario:
Production Incident #15: An online A/B experimentation platform detected anomalous metric movements and sample ratio mismatch (SRM) in Exploratory Data Analysis & Feature Engineering. In an active experiment evaluating 'Target Encoding, Target Leakage and Out-of-Fold Encoding', p-values were artificially deflated, and variance was underestimated by 60%.

### Engineering Challenge:
Which statistical remediation correctly eliminates false positive statistical significance in this 'Target Encoding, Target Leakage and Out-of-Fold Encoding' evaluation?

options.text: Run standard two-sample independent t-tests treating every individual page event as an independent observation.
Drop all users who logged in more than once during the experimental trial window.
Apply cluster-robust standard errors or Delta method variance corrections to account for intra-cluster correlation across repeated user sessions.
Increase the alpha threshold from 0.05 to 0.20 to accept the observed metric variance.

answer_explanation: In Exploratory Data Analysis & Feature Engineering, analyzing session-level observations when randomization occurs at the user level introduces intra-cluster correlation. Using naive standard errors severely underestimates variance. Cluster-robust variance estimators or the Delta method restore nominal false positive rates.
reference_solution: Recommended Remediation: Option C. Rationale: In Exploratory Data Analysis & Feature Engineering, analyzing session-level observations when randomization occurs at the user level introduces intra-cluster correlation. Using naive standard errors severely underestimates variance. Cluster-robust variance estimators or the Delta method restore nominal false positive rates.
